author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Test name `processFindFormPageBelowOneClampsToFirstPage` names the production method being called, not the behavior under test. The brief (§ Test Naming) mandates the BDD school `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward — this test was added in this slice and is fully in scope. A name like `theOwnerListShouldRenderFirstPageWhenPageParamIsBelowOne` would survive renaming the controller method and communicate what must remain true.
findings.fix: Rename the test method to follow `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`, e.g. `theOwnerListShouldRenderFirstPageWhenPageParamIsBelowOne`.

findings.description: The new test body has no blank-line separator between the Arrange phase (lines 153-154) and the Act/Assert phase (line 155). The brief (§ Four-Phase Test Structure) requires phases to be separated by blank lines. The existing `processFindFormWithWhitespaceOnlyLastNameReturnsAllOwners` test at line 181 models the correct style; the new test copies the no-blank-line shape of `processFindFormSuccess` instead, which is pre-existing debt the brief does not require sweeping but does require new tests to avoid.
findings.fix: Insert a blank line between the `when(...)` stub line and the `mockMvc.perform(...)` assertion line.

findings.description: The new test constructs `new Owner()` directly. The brief (§ Test Data Construction, Factory Methods) prohibits raw constructor calls in tests written from 2026-07-31 onward — a slice that adds a test must write it behind a factory from the start. `new Owner()` here is an anonymous irrelevant fixture; the sweep found three other occurrences at lines 146, 183, and 270 but those are pre-existing debt excluded by the brief's date rule. Only line 153, added in this slice, is in scope.
findings.fix: Replace `new Owner()` with a call to an anonymous factory, e.g. `createAnOwner()`, following the brief's anonymous-factory pattern.

findings.description: Only `page=0` is tested. The clamping fix applies to all values below 1: `page=-1` and `page=-100` previously crashed with `PageRequest.of(negative, size)` just as `page=0` did. The brief (§ Edge Case Coverage) asks for `@ParameterizedTest` with `@CsvSource` when a family of inputs shares the same expected behavior. The boundary is a single class (any int < 1), so a parameterized method with three CSV rows covering 0, -1, and a large negative value would exhaust it without duplicating test logic.
findings.fix: Convert to `@ParameterizedTest @ValueSource(ints = {0, -1, -99})` and update the method signature to accept the page-param int, passing it to `get("/owners?page=" + page)`.

approved_aspects: The test genuinely reproduces the defect: GET /owners?page=0 would have triggered PageRequest.of(-1, size) before the fix, which Spring Data rejects with IllegalArgumentException; the test red-greens correctly.
All 16 OwnerControllerTests pass after the fix with 0 failures and 0 skips.

The mock usage follows the brief's sanctioned pattern: the in-process MockMvc harness stands in for HTTP transport; the owners-repository stub is tolerated pre-existing usage; no new mock-framework coupling was introduced beyond what the adjacent tests already use.
The production fix is minimal and correctly placed at the entry of processFindForm so every code path downstream receives a valid page value.
The page=0 boundary is the exact value that surfaces the off-by-one: it is a real bug example, not invented data.
